new_claims.claim: Excelsior III jump, 16 Aug 1960, from 102,800 ft (31,300 m) = 19.5 mi ('nineteen miles up')
Right glove pressurization malfunctioned during the ascent; right hand swelled to twice its normal size
Free fall 4 min 36 s ('over four and a half minutes'); DFC citation says 4:38
Airliners cruise around 35,000 ft (reference line only)

new_claims.basis: MR-2 31 Jan 1961 vs Shepard's Freedom 7, 5 May 1961 (first crewed American flight)

new_claims.claim: Apogee 157 mi vs 115 planned; faster than the planned 4,400 mph
Landed 422 mi downrange, an overshoot of the planned landing area by 130 mi
Heat shield punched two holes in the pressure bulkhead; about 800 lb of seawater aboard ('started filling with seawater')
Ham in good condition (small nose abrasion, dehydrated) ('Ham was fine')

scripts.P4-kittinger: [tense] This man jumped from the edge of space. In nineteen sixty, Joe Kittinger stepped off a balloon nineteen miles up. [curious] On the way up, his glove failed, and his right hand swelled to twice its size. [surprised] He jumped anyway, and fell for over four and a half minutes.
scripts.P6-ham: [curious] This chimp flew to space before any American astronaut. NASA launched Ham higher and faster than planned. [tense] His capsule splashed down a hundred and thirty miles off target, and started filling with seawater. [surprised] When they opened it, Ham was fine.
